Subject: SDK integration kickoff + schema questions

Hi Marissa —

Great call this morning. Thanks for walking us through Redwood Dedicated and the routing options. A few follow-ups from our engineering team to help scope the POC:

- SDK auth: we need clarity on OAuth vs API key for Private deployments (VPC). Can the SDK do short-lived tokens via our IdP?
- Chat vs completions: for our use-case (multi-turn support + tool calling for ticket lookups) should we use the chat endpoints or the completions API with structured output?
- Tokenization / max_tokens: how do you recommend we plan prompt + context sizing given our ~8k token transcripts?
- Stop sequences & streaming: we want to stream partial responses but enforce a deterministic stop when tool output begins — is that supported?

Can you loop in the SDK/infra person who can confirm these details and share a sample request/response schema?

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Platform Engineer, Zephyr AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SDK integration kickoff + schema questions

Thanks Daniel — good questions. Recap and next steps below. I copied Dev to answer the protocol/SDK specifics.

Recap / recommended POC approach:
- Auth: For Private (VPC) we support API keys and short-lived JWTs backed by the customer IdP via our token exchange. The SDK supports obtaining short-lived tokens when you provide a service account and IdP metadata — works with SAML/OIDC flows.
- Endpoint choice: For multi-turn + tool calling, use our chat endpoint (structured output + function/tool calling). Completions can work but you lose the explicit turn-state primitives we expose in chat.
- Token planning: start with a 12k token budget (8k transcript + 2k prompt + 2k response ceiling) and iterate. We provide token-usage estimates in the SDK response headers.
- Streaming + stop: streaming is supported for chat. We emit a stream of delta tokens and a final 'tool_call' event when structured tool output is emitted; you can configure stop tokens but for tool calls we recommend using the structured tool_call field in the schema instead of stop sequences.

Next steps:
1) Dev: share sample JSON request/response for chat + tool calling and an SDK auth example.
2) Marissa/Zephyr: confirm POC scope and timeline — proposed week of 3/29.
3) Daniel: send any compliance checklist items we should prep for Private.

I'll schedule a 30-minute technical sync for next week.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-19T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK integration kickoff + schema questions

Hey Daniel —

Attaching a concise reference below (also attached as rsp-schema-proposal.pdf). Sample chat request (streaming-enabled) and response (tool_call + structured output):

--- SAMPLE REQUEST (chat endpoint; JSON over REST) ---
POST /v1/chat?stream=true
Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant that can call the ticket_lookup tool."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Show me the last 3 tickets for user@example.com"}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {"name": "ticket_lookup", "input_schema": {"email": "string"}}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "temperature": 0.0
}

Notes: streaming=true will return a token delta stream and special events (schema below).

--- SAMPLE RESPONSE STREAM (token deltas + events) ---
data: {"delta": "Looking up ", "type": "token"}
data: {"delta": "tickets for ", "type": "token"}
data: {"event": "tool_call", "tool": "ticket_lookup", "input": {"email": "user@example.com"}}
data: {"event": "tool_response", "tool": "ticket_lookup", "output": {"tickets": [{"id": "T-123","summary":"Login failure","created":"2026-03-10"}]}}
data: {"delta": "Found 1 ticket.", "type": "token"}
data: {"event": "done"}

Important bits and recommendations:
- Tokenization: the SDK exposes a token_count helper that mirrors the model tokenizer. Use it to pre-calc prompt + context size. For very large histories, use our prefix/KV cache or only send embeddings+retrieval results.
- max_tokens: set to the response ceiling. The sum prompt_tokens + max_tokens must be <= model_max (model dependent). We recommend server-side enforcement in the SDK so you don't hit 413 errors.
- stop sequences vs structured events: stop sequences still work for free-form completions, but for tool calling prefer the structured tool_call/tool_response events — deterministic and easier to parse in a stream.
- Streaming semantics: the stream includes token deltas and discrete events. The SDK will surface events as typed callbacks (onToken, onEvent). You can buffer tokens between tool_call/event transitions and flush to the UI.

Auth examples:
- API key: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> (long-lived)
- Short-lived JWT: Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN> (we provide a token-exchange API: you POST your IdP assertion to /v1/exchange and we return a short-lived token scoped to the customer/project).

Let me know if you want a runnable curl + Node SDK snippet and I'll paste it.

- Dev
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dev — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our infra/security lead:

- Token exchange: can we restrict scopes on the short-lived token to only the chat endpoint and specific model names? We want least-privilege.
- Embeddings/reranker: for retrieval-augmented generation we plan to store embeddings in our vector DB. Does Redwood return embedding vectors alongside the chat response, or do we need a separate embeddings call?
- Determinism: in streaming mode, are the token delta events ordered and guaranteed (i.e., can we rely on event order vs. reconstructing from tokens)?

If those look OK we'll confirm the POC timeline. Also, please send the curl + Node SDK snippet for token-exchange and streaming.

—Daniel

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-22T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK integration kickoff + schema questions

Hi Daniel — following up on the outstanding items:

- Token scopes: yes. Short-lived tokens support scope claims limiting endpoints (chat, embeddings) and model names. We can also restrict via project IDs and network IP allowlists in Private deployments.
- Embeddings: embeddings are a separate API call. For RAG we recommend generating embeddings server-side and storing them in your DB; you can pass retrieved passages back in the chat request. We do offer an optional batch embeddings helper in the SDK.
- Streaming determinism: yes — token delta events are strictly ordered per request and you can rely on event order. Tool events are emitted inline in the stream at the exact logical position where the model triggered the tool call.

Attached is a curl + Node snippet (see rsp-schema-proposal.pdf) and a proposed POC plan for week of 3/29.

If that works, Marissa will send an NDA/POC SOW and we'll lock in a technical kickoff.

Best,
Lauren
